newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close easier in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close easier in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly lower in trading which was dull and limited to a few inexpensive, liquid shares, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.31 points down at 589.97. Aitken Spence & Co fell 20 rupees to 90, Hayleys two to 175.
Turnover was 12.3 million rupees on turnover of 317,334 shares.

"The market has no sparkle due to the lack of small retail investors who move prices," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities. Such investors would only return in the new year, he added.
Quantities of 23,000 Blue Diamonds at 10 rupees, 19,300 Hayleys at 175, 20,000 Lanka Ceramic at 30.50, 22,400 Seylan Bank at 25.25 and 37,900 Grain Elevators at 10, were the main trades of the day.

"The irony is that even when you can buy in quantity, there are no sellers," said Abeysekera. He said sellers believe that December, which is generally a slack period, is more a time for buying than selling.
A parcel of 1.7 million Horana Plantations at 24 rupees, introduced on Monday on an all-or-none basis, remains on bid. The parcel will be concluded on Wednesday.
